The Police Sub Inspector of Madivala P.S has submitted the Charge Sheet against the accused No.1 to 5 for the offences punishable Under Secs.498A of IPC r/w Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
2.

The brief facts of the Prosecution case are as follows:
That the accused No.1 married C.W.1 on 27.02.2010 as per hindu rites and customs and at the time of marriage the accused No.1 to 5 demanded and received dowry of Rs.65,000/- cash and gold ornaments weighing 115 grams.

Further after marriage while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house at No.32,
VidyaJyothi Nagar, 5 th cross, 11th main road, Hongasandra, Madivala the accused persons demanded C.W.1 to get additional dowry of Rs.25,000/- from her parents and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty.

Thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable U/Sec. 498A of IPC r/w Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.

sentences.text: On the basis of the Statement of CW-1, the Madivala Police have registered a case under Crime No.218/2013 for the offences punishable U/s 498A of IPC r/w Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act against the accused No.1 to 5 and submitted the FIR before the court.

Thereafter the investigating officer visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar and recorded the statement of witnesses on completion of the investigation, the Charge Sheet has been filed against the accused for the offence punishable Under Sec.498A of IPC r/w Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
On the receipt of the police report, this court has taken cognizance for the said offence.
4. On the appearance of the accused No.1 to 5, the accused No.1 to 5 were enlarged on bail.
The copies of prosecution papers were furnished to the accused No.1 to 5 as contemplated U/Sec. 207 of Cr.P.C.
After hearing both the parties, the charge was framed against the accused No.1 to 5 for the offences punishable U/Sec. 498A of IPC r/w Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act and read over to them.
Accused No.1 to 5 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

Hence, the matter was posted for evidence.
5.

In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 to 5 , the prosecution has got examined four witnesses as PW-1 to 4, out of the total charge sheet witnesses as CW-1 to 9 and got marked nine documents as Ex.P1 to P.9.
It was reported that C.W.3 is dead.
Subsequently summons, NBW and proclamation was issued to C.W.4 to 7 .

Inspite of issuance of NBW and proclamation to C.W.4 too 7 the police have failed to secure the above said witnesses, hence by rejecting the prayer of Learned Sr.APP this Court dropped the recording of evidence of C.W.4 to 7.
It was reported that the accused No.4 is dead and as such case against accused No.4 is abated.
After closure of prosecution evidence, the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 are examined U/S 313(1)(b) of Cr.P.C.
The evidence is read over separately to the accused.
The accused No.1 to 3 and 5 denied all such incriminating circumstances as false.
Accused No.1 to 3 and 5 did not choose to explain anything during their examination.

Accused No.1 to 3 and 5 did not choose to adduce defence evidence and no documents are got marked on behalf of accused No.1 to 3 and 5.
6.
I have heard the arguments addressed by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor and learned advocate for the accused.

7. On going through the facts and circumstances of the prosecution case, the following points would arise for my consideration :
POINTS 1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 married C.W.1 on 27/2/2010 as per Hindu rites and customs and at the time of marriage the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 along with deceased accused No.4 demanded and received cash of Rs.65,000/- and gold ornaments weighing 115 grams as dowry and thereby the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 have committed the offence of "receiving and demanding dowry"

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house at No.32, VidyaJyothi Nagar, 5th cross, 11th main road, Hongasandra, Madivala the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 along with deceased accused No.4 demanded C.W.1 to get additional dowry of Rs.25,000/- from her parents and subjected C.W.1 to physical and mental cruelty and thereby the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 subjected C.W.1 to cruelty and have committed the offence of "extending physical and mental cruelty" punishable u/s 498(A) r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
3. What Order ?
8. My findings to the above Points are as under:
 Point No.1 and 2 : In the Negative.
 Point No.3 : As per final order,
 For the following: -
 R EAS O N S 9. Point No.1 and 2:- Both these points are inter linked with each other and also similar evidence is led on both the points, I have taken all these points together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and discussion.

It is allegation that the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 have committed the offences punishable under Section 498(A) of Indian Penal Code r/w Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
10.

In order to prove its case, prosecution has got examined 04 witnesses namely C.W.1/P.W.1-Smt.Jyothi, C.W.2/P.W.2 -Smt.Manjula, C.W.8/P.W.3-Ramesh-Head constable and C.W.9/P.W.4-G.T.Srinivas-PSI.
11.

It is the case of the prosecution that the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 demanded and received received cash of Rs.65,000/- and gold ornaments weighing 115 grams as dowry and after marriage while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house at Hongasandra, the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 along with deceased accused No.4 demanded C.W.1 to get additional dowry of Rs.25,000/- from her parents and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty.
12.
The prosecution in support of its case examined C.W.1/Smt.Jyothi as P.W.1.

P.W.1 in her chief examination has deposed that the accused no.1 is her husband, accused No.2, 3 and 5 are the father ,
mother and sister of accused No.1 and accused No.4 is the brother in law of accused No.1.

She deposed that her marriage with accused No.1 was solemnized on 18.01.2010 and during marriage golden ornaments weighing 120 grams and cash of Rs.65,000/- were given as dowry to the accused persons.

After marriage while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house at ThovinaKere,
Jyothi vs Manjegowda on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127339026/
4 Channarayapatna the accused No.1 to 5 extended physical and mental harassment towards her by demanding additional dowry and tried to set her ablaze by pouring kerosene over her.

She further deposed that she went to the police station at Channarayapatna and lodged complaint, but said complaint was not registered and then panchayath was convened and she went back to the matrimonial house .

13. Further she deposed that herself and accused No.1 came to Hongasandra at Bengaluru and the other accused persons came to their residence and started to harass her for additional dowry and the accused persons assaulted her sister and during their stay at Bengaluru the accused No.1 was not paying house rent properly and the advance of the rented house was given by her parents.

P.W.1 further deposed that when she was at her parental house after delivery, the accused No.1 came there and took away her 03 month old baby along with him and told her that he would not give back the baby and he would marry again.
She further deposed that she lodged complaint at Channarayapatna P.S. and then panchayath was convened again.
Further PW.1 deposed that when herself and accused were residing at Hongasandra, Bengaluru the accused persons pledged her jewelry and assaulted her by demanding her to get additional dowry.
Further PW..1 deposed that she lodged complaint at Madivala Police station as per Ex.P.1.
On the next day police came to the house and conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P.2.

She deposed that she produced the copies of jewelry receipts which are marked as Ex.P.8 and 9.
14.

The counsel for accused cross examined the P.W.1 at length and during cross examination the P.W.1 admitted that accused no.1 is her distant relative, she denied the suggestion that her marriage with the accused no.1 is a love marriage and she denied the suggestion that the accused no.1 was staying at their house prior to marriage.
She deposed that she did not write the contents of Ex.P.1-complaint, but she got written the complaint through her sister Shobha.
She deposed that Rs.65,000/- was given as dowry to the accused persons in the presence of her parent and relatives of accused persons.
P.W.1 deposed that her father is alive and Rs.65,000/- was given to the parents of accused No.1 by her parents and brother of her father.
She denied the suggestion that they have not given Rs.65,000/- as dowry.
She denied the suggestion that she does not know the name of father of accused No.1, since her marriage with the accused No.1 was a love marriage.

She further deposed that she has produced the copies of the jewelry purchase receipts before this court, since she has produced the original receipts before the Family Court wherein she is seeking maintenance.
She deposed that she had handed over the original receipts to the police, but the police took the copies of the same and returned the original receipts to her.
She denied the suggestion that she has created the receipts for the purpose of this case.
She further deposed that she lodged complaint regarding harassment extended to her when her baby was 03 months old and she has not produced any documents to show that.
She denied the suggestion that she is deposing false evidence P.W.1 further deposed that she has not produced any documents to show that they were residing at Hongasandra.
She admitted the suggestion that she has mentioned in the complaint that her marriage with the accused No.1 is a love marriage.
She denied the suggestion that she is deposing false evidence regarding the dowry harassment against accused persons and she has filed false case against accused persons.

5 15.
The prosecution examined C.W.2/Smt.Manjula ie mother of C.W.1 as P.W.2.
P.W.2 in her chief examination has deposed that the C.W.1 is her elder daughter and she was married to accused no.1 and after marriage the C.W.1 was residing with the accused persons at Govinakere.

P.W.2 further deposed that during marriage talks the accused persons demanded golden ornaments weighing 120 grams and cash of Rs.65,000/- and as per the demand the accused No.1 and 2 were given Rs.65,000/- cash and 120 grams of gold ornaments as dowry.

After marriage while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house the accused extended physical and mental harassment towards her by demanding additional dowry and every time panchayath was held and the matter was settled.

16. Further she deposed that after the birth of a baby the accused persons did not allow C.W.1 to their house and they pledged the gold ornaments of her daughter and when her 2 nd daughter came to the house of C.W.1 and accused No.1 at Hongasandra, Bengaluru the accused No.1 assaulted C.W.3 and C.W.1 lodged complaint.
17.
The counsel for accused cross examined the P.W.2 at length and during cross examination the P.W.2 deposed that they are residing in Bengaluru since the last 15 years and her husband is alive.
She admitted that accused no.1 is her relative and the accused No.1 was residing in thier house even prior to the marriage with C.W.1.
She denied the suggestion that the accused No.1 was not her relative.

She deposed that prior to marriage the accused No.1 was not going to work and her daughter ie C.W.1 was working in a Garments factory She denied the suggestion that the accused No.1 was in love with C.W.1 and the marriage of C.W.1 with accused no.1 was a love marriage.
She further deposed that the marriage talks took place at the house of accused No.1 and 15 members from their side had attended the marriage talks.

One Kempananjegowda, Rajegowda,
Devarajegowda, Basavaraju, Dorai, Devaraju, Ramegowda and 05 others attended the marriage talks.
She deposed that she does not remember the names of other 5 people.
She denied the suggestion that she has not given statement regarding going for the marriage talks.
P.W.2 further deposed that the C.W.1 and accused resided at Govinakere for 2 years after marriage and she has not produced any documents to show that a complaint was lodged at Channarayapatna.
She denied the suggestion that no galata took place and as such no complaint was lodged.
She deposed that she has the original jewelry purchase receipts and she denied the suggestion that the reciepts are created for the sake of this case.
She denied the suggestion that there was no demand for dowry or dowry harassment since the marriage of C.W.1 and accused No.1 was a love marriage.
She admitted the suggestion that the accused No.2 to 5 are residing at different villages and she denied the suggestion that they have not harassed CW.1.

18. C.W.8/PW.3-Ramesh-Head constable in his evidence deposed that on 23.03.2013 he was directed to trace out the accused persons and accordingly he received credible information that the accused no.1 was at Hongasandra and he went there and arrested the accused No.1 and produced him at the PS.
The counsel for accused cross examined the witness and during cross examination this witness withstood to his version stated in the chief examination.

19. C.W.9/P.W.4- G.T.Srinivas CPI- in his evidence deposed that on 22.03.2013 while he was doing duty as PSI at Madivala P.S C.W.1 lodged a written complaint against the accused as per Ex.P.1 and he registered the crime and sent FIR to the court.

Further he deposed that he visited spot and Jyothi vs Manjegowda on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127339026/
6 conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P.2.

sentences.text: Further he deposed regarding the investigation carried out by him.
The counsel for accused cross examined the witness and during cross examination this witness withstood to his version stated in the chief examination.
20. The accused is in total denial of the case of the prosecution and denied the demand for dowry and dowry harassment as the marriage of accused No.1 and C.W.1 was a love marriage.

21. On perusal of the entire evidence and material placed on record it is evident to note that prosecution has not made efforts to prove that the accused extended physical and mental harassment to C.W.1.
22.
As per Sec. 498A of the IPC.

"Sec.498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty-Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term,
which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation: for the purpose of this section.

"
cruelty" means- (a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand".
23. Herein this case it is worth to note that the father of the complainant has not been cited as a charge sheet witness.
More over in the evidence of P.W.2, she has stated that her husband is alive.
But doubt arises in the mind of the court as to why he is not cited as a charge sheet witness.
The father of the complainant is not been made a witness depicts a doubt as to the case of the prosecution regarding giving of dowry as demanded by the accused.
24. The allegation that the accused taking 120 grams of gold and Rs.65,000/- from C.W.1/P.W.1 is not proved by furnishing sufficient documentary evidence.
The C.W.1/P.W.1 herself admits the suggestion that she has not produced documents to show that they gave golden ornaments weighing 120 grams and Rs.65,000/- to the accused.
The copies of the jewelry purchase receipts are produced.

Further more it creates a doubt as to why the father of C.W.1 is not cited as a witness Jyothi vs Manjegowda on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127339026/
7

though he gave dowry as demanded by the accused and performed the marriage of C.W.1 and accused No.1.
25.
Further the P.W.1 admitted that accused no.1 is her distant relative and her marriage with the accused no.1 is a love marriage.
She deposed that Rs.65,000/- was given as dowry to the accused persons in the presence of her parents and relatives of accused persons.
P.W.1 deposed that her father is alive and Rs.65,000/- was given to the parents of accused No.1 by her parents and brother of her father.
Doubt arises as to why the father of C.W.1 is not cited as a charge sheet witness and examined by the prosecution to prove the aspect of accused demanding and receiving dowry.
26. It is pertinent to note that the name of father of accused No.1 is mentioned as Rajanna in the marriage invitation card.

Whereas the name of accused no.2 ie father of accused No.1 is mentioned as Byregowda in the charge sheet and the P.W.2 in her statement before police has stated the name of father of accused no.1 as Byregowda.
This also creates a doubt.
This clearly shows that the P.W.1 is not clear with the name of her father in law ie accused No.2.
Probably the accused No.2 was not residing with the accused No.1 and C.W.1.

The P.W.2 being the mother of C.W.1 has admitted in the cross examination that the accused No.2 to 5 were residing at their native places and different from the accused No.1 and C.W.1.
27.
The prosecution has not produced sufficient documentary evidence to show that the parents of C.W.1 gave jewelry of 120 grams as demanded.

P.W1 deposed that she has produced the copies of the jewelry purchase receipts before this court, since she has produced the original receipts before the Family Court wherein she is seeking maintenance.

She deposed that she had handed over the original receipts to the police, but the police took the copies of the same and returned the original receipts to her.
28.
P.W.1 deposed that she lodged complaint regarding harassment extended to her when her baby was 03 months old and she has not produced any documents to prove the said contention.

29. The defence of the accused is total denial of the case of the prosection, as the marriage of accused No.1 and C.W.1 was a love marriage and same is admitted by the P.W.1 in her evidence and same is stated in the complaint of C.W.1.
The P.W.1 and P.W.2 admit that the accused No.1 is their relative and he was residing in their house even prior to the marriage.

30. In the instant case, no where in the complaint or evidence the C.W.1 has complained of harassment to an extent wherein she was driven to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) or harassment with a view to coerce her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property.

The allegations made in the complaint or her evidence indicates that the accused committed the offence U/s 498A of IPC.
31.

Further more on the issue of appreciation of evidence of interested witnesses, Dalip Singh Vs.
State of Punjab, AIR 1953 SC 364 -1954 SCR 145, is one of the earliest cases on the point.

In that case, it was held as follows:

sentences.text: "A witness is normally to be considered independent unless he or she springs from sources which are likely to be tainted and that usually means unless the witness has cause, such as enmity against the accused, to wish to implicate him falsely.
Ordinarily, a close relative would be the last to screen the real culprit and falsely implicate an innocent person.

It is true, when feelings run high and there is personal cause for enmity, that there is a tendency to drag in an innocent person against whom a witness has a grudge along with the guilty, but foundation must be laid for such a criticism and the mere fact of relationship far from being a foundation is often a sure guarantee of truth.
32. It is pertinent to note that apart from the interested witness ie C.W.1/PW.1 and C.W.2/P.W.2, no other independent witnesses have been examined.

Under these circumstances, in the reported decisions it is held as under:
" Where the witnesses are interested, their evidence should be scrutinized with great caution"
The law laid down in the said decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand.
33.

Further relying on the decision reported in 1999 Crl.L.J 19 (SC) (Sanspal Singh Vs State of Delhi)
-It is evident that public witnesses were available and could have been associated to witness the recovery.

entities.text: 1999 Crl.L.J 19 (SC) (Sanspal Singh Vs State of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It would have been a different matter altogether, had there been No public witness available or none was willing to associate here as stated above, public witnesses were available but No explanation on these lines is forthcoming.
Thus it would be unsafe to maintain conviction of the appellant for the offences charged"
The above said decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand.
34. It is pertinent to note that the father of C.W.1 has not been examined by the prosection.
No reason is forthcoming as to why he is not cited as a charge sheet witness, though he is a prime witness who attended the marriage talks and gave dowry as demanded by the accused.
Further more the neighbors to the house where C.W.1 and accused No.1 were residing are not examined to prove the harassment extended by the accused.
Non examination of these independent witnesses can also be fatal to the case of prosecution.
Non examination of father of C.W.1 and independent witnesses to prove the aspect of dowry harassment extended by the accused is a serious lapse on the part of the prosecution.
P.W.3 and 4 being the police witnesses have deposed regarding the investigation carried out by them and their evidence alone is not sufficient to prove the case of the prosecution.
35. Furthermore the decision reported in (2017)11 SCC 195- Yogesh Singh Vs Mahabeer Singh and others..

At para 16 Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under:
"16.

Another golden thread which runs through the web of the administration of justice in criminal cases is that if two views are possible on the evidence adduced in Jyothi vs Manjegowda on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127339026/
9 the case, one pointing to the guilt of the accused and the other to his innocence, the view which is favourable to the accused should be adopted"
The above said decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand.
36.

sentences.text: For the reasons stated above, it is clear that number of serious doubts arises in the mind of the court as to the evidence and circumstances of the case on hand.
Under these circumstances, no doubt the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 are entitled for benefit of doubt.

Hence this court held that the evidence placed on record is not pointing out towards guilt of the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 only and accused No.1 to 3 and 5 as a matter of right is entitled for benefit of doubt and prosecution failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

37. Point No.3: - In view of the findings of point No.1 and 2, this court proceed to pass the following;
 O RDE R

Acting U/Sec.248(1) of Cr.P.C.
 accused No.1 to 3 and 5 is acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec. 498(A) of IPC.
and 5 and Surety bonds shall stand canceled.
Bail bond executed U/s 437(A) of Cr.P.C.shall be continued.

opennyai_summary.issue:
7. On going through the facts and circumstances of the prosecution case, the following points would arise for my consideration :
POINTS 1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 married C.W.1 on 27/2/2010 as per Hindu rites and customs and at the time of marriage the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 along with deceased accused No.4 demanded and received cash of Rs.65,000/- and gold ornaments weighing 115 grams as dowry and thereby the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 have committed the offence of "receiving and demanding dowry"
Jyothi vs Manjegowda on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127339026/
3 punishable u/s 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
2.
Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house at No.32, VidyaJyothi Nagar, 5th cross, 11th main road, Hongasandra, Madivala the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 along with deceased accused No.4 demanded C.W.1 to get additional dowry of Rs.25,000/- from her parents and subjected C.W.1 to physical and mental cruelty and thereby the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 subjected C.W.1 to cruelty and have committed the offence of "extending physical and mental cruelty" punishable u/s 498(A) r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
3. What Order ?
8. My findings to the above Points are as under:
 Point No.1 and 2 : In the Negative.
 Point No.3 : As per final order,
 For the following: -
 R EAS O N S 9. Point No.1 and 2:- Both these points are inter linked with each other and also similar evidence is led on both the points, I have taken all these points together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and discussion.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The father of the complainant is not been made a witness depicts a doubt as to the case of the prosecution regarding giving of dowry as demanded by the accused.
The P.W.1 and P.W.2 admit that the accused No.1 is their relative and he was residing in their house even prior to the marriage.
30. In the instant case, no where in the complaint or evidence the C.W.1 has complained of harassment to an extent wherein she was driven to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) or harassment with a view to coerce her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property.
The allegations made in the complaint or her evidence indicates that the accused committed the offence U/s 498A of IPC.
31.
Further more on the issue of appreciation of evidence of interested witnesses, Dalip Singh Vs.
State of Punjab, AIR 1953 SC 364 -1954 SCR 145, is one of the earliest cases on the point.
No reason is forthcoming as to why he is not cited as a charge sheet witness, though he is a prime witness who attended the marriage talks and gave dowry as demanded by the accused.
Further more the neighbors to the house where C.W.1 and accused No.1 were residing are not examined to prove the harassment extended by the accused.
Non examination of these independent witnesses can also be fatal to the case of prosecution.
Non examination of father of C.W.1 and independent witnesses to prove the aspect of dowry harassment extended by the accused is a serious lapse on the part of the prosecution.
Hence this court held that the evidence placed on record is not pointing out towards guilt of the accused No.1 to 3 and 5 only and accused No.1 to 3 and 5 as a matter of right is entitled for benefit of doubt and prosecution failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
